reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 and E2 discuss corrosion and oxidation resistance in as-cast or single-phase alloys without demonstrating heat-treatment-induced dual-phase microstructures or precipitate-mediated simultaneous improvements. E3 shows simultaneous strength and corrosion resistance in an amorphous film, not a dual-phase bulk alloy with precipitates, and does not address oxidation resistance. No cited passage provides evidence for the claimed mechanism or the comparative advantage of a dual-phase over single-phase state.
premises: Nanoscale intermetallic precipitates can be formed in lightweight HEAs by heat treatment
These precipitates act as dispersion-strengthening agents that impede dislocation motion
The precipitates act as physical barriers to diffusion of corrosive species and oxygen
A dual-phase microstructure with precipitates will simultaneously improve strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance over a single-phase state
